examples.ko: 그 가수가 갑자기 인기 스타로 급부상했어요.
examples.en: That singer suddenly rose to become a popular star.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술의 급부상이 시장을 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: The sudden rise of the new technology is changing the market.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 우승 후보로 급부상하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is suddenly emerging as a title contender.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 맛집 거리로 급부상한 곳이에요.
examples.en: This neighborhood is a place that has suddenly become a famous food street.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 그 회사의 급부상을 크게 다뤘어요.
examples.en: The news covered that company's sudden rise at length.

examples.ko: 작년에 급부상한 배우가 올해는 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: The actor who suddenly rose to fame last year appears in a movie this year.

explain: 주로 '급부상하다'로 써요. 사람, 회사, 나라가 짧은 시간에 눈에 띄게 올라올 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 천천히 올라오면 '성장하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Mostly used as the verb 급부상하다. It is common in the news for a person, company or country that stands out in a short time. For slower growth, 성장하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: My grandmother washed the bellflower roots clean for me.
I caught a cold, so I drank bellflower root tea.
I bought a bag of bellflower roots at the market.
The seasoned bellflower my mom made is really delicious.
Lots of purple bellflowers bloomed on the mountain.

examples.ko: 도라지는 쓴맛이 조금 나지만 몸에 좋아요.
examples.en: Bellflower root tastes a little bitter, but it is good for you.

explain: 한국에서는 꽃보다 뿌리 나물과 약재로 더 많이 알려져 있어요. 목이 아플 때 도라지 차나 도라지청을 먹는 사람이 많아요. '도라지타령'이라는 유명한 민요도 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea it is known more as a root vegetable and herbal remedy than as a flower. Many people drink 도라지 tea or eat 도라지청 for a sore throat. There is also a famous folk song called 도라지타령.

examples.en: I divide the cake equally into eight pieces.
The teacher divided the paper equally into three.
I will divide the field equally into four parts.
I shape the equally divided dough into rounds.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 선분을 등분하는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In math class I learned how to divide a line segment equally.
I split my allowance into two equal parts and saved it.

explain: '몇 개로 등분하다'처럼 같은 크기로 나눌 때만 써요. 크기가 달라도 되는 '나누다'와 달리 조각이 모두 똑같아야 해요. 수학이나 요리 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used only when dividing into equal sizes, as in 몇 개로 등분하다. Unlike 나누다, which allows unequal parts, 등분하다 needs every part to be the same size. It shows up often in math and cooking instructions.

examples.en: The hot broth warms my body.
The floor is nicely warm, so it is good for lying down.
They just took out fresh warm bread at the bakery.
On cold days I drink tea hot.
The hand warmer is nice and warm.
If the bath water is nicely hot, your tiredness goes away.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 데일 만큼 뜨거울 때도 쓰지만, '따끈하다'는 기분 좋게 따뜻한 정도예요. 국, 빵, 방바닥, 목욕물처럼 먹거나 몸에 닿는 것에 많이 써요. '따뜻하다'보다 조금 더 열이 있는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 뜨겁다 can mean hot enough to burn, but 따끈하다 is pleasantly hot. It is used for things you eat or touch, like soup, bread, a heated floor or a bath. It feels a little hotter than 따뜻하다.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.

examples.ko: 엄마가 손으로 짠 머플러를 선물해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mom gave me a scarf she knitted by hand.
In winter, just one scarf keeps you warm.

examples.ko: 이 빨간 머플러는 어느 코트에나 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This red scarf goes well with any coat.
My scarf almost blew away in the wind.
I left my scarf on the subway.

explain: 목에 두르는 목도리를 말하고, 일상에서는 '목도리'가 더 흔해요. '머플러'는 패션 쪽에서 조금 멋을 내는 느낌으로 써요. 자동차 배기 장치를 뜻하는 '머플러'도 있어서 문맥으로 구분해요.
explain_en: It means a neck scarf, but 목도리 is more common in daily life. 머플러 sounds a bit more fashionable. 머플러 can also mean a car's exhaust muffler, so context tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: I watched amazing stunts at the circus.

examples.ko: 강아지가 공을 받는 묘기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The puppy showed a trick of catching a ball.
That player performs tricks with a soccer ball.
The children clapped for the stunt.
I practice every day to enter the stunt contest.
The bicycle stunts were really thrilling.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 연습해서 보여 주는 놀라운 재주예요. '재능'은 타고난 능력이고, '묘기'는 눈앞에서 보여 주는 기술이에요. '묘기를 부리다'나 '묘기를 보여 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is an amazing skill that a person or animal has practiced and shows off. 재능 is natural talent, while 묘기 is a skill performed in front of people. It goes with verbs like 묘기를 부리다 and 묘기를 보여 주다.

examples.ko: 그 아이를 문제아라고 부르면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not call that child a troublemaker.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 저는 선생님 속을 썩이는 문제아였어요.
examples.en: As a kid I was a troublemaker who worried my teachers.

examples.ko: 영화에는 문제아가 선생님을 만나 달라지는 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: The movie tells of a troublemaker who changes after meeting a teacher.
I heard he had a hard time after being labeled a troublemaker at school.
A counseling program for problem kids has been created.
He changed from a troublemaker to a model student.

explain: 행동 때문에 학교나 집에서 걱정을 끼치는 아이를 말해요. 듣는 아이에게는 상처가 될 수 있어서 직접 앞에서 부르는 말로는 잘 안 써요. 반대말로는 '모범생'을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a child whose behavior worries school or family. It can hurt the child, so it is rarely used to someone's face. Its common opposite is 모범생.

examples.en: Willow trees stand in a long row along the river.
When the wind blew, the willow branches swayed.
In spring, new shoots come up on willow trees.
We rested in the shade of a willow tree.
The willow beside the park pond is beautiful.
I heard people used willow bark to bring down fevers long ago.

explain: 가지가 아래로 늘어지는 나무로, 물가에서 많이 볼 수 있어요. '버들'이나 '수양버들'도 비슷한 나무를 가리켜요. 한국 옛 그림과 노래에서 봄을 나타내는 나무로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A tree with drooping branches, often seen near water. 버들 and 수양버들 refer to similar trees. In old Korean paintings and songs it often stands for spring.

examples.en: Sunlight comes into the balcony well.
I dried the laundry in the warm sun.

examples.ko: 고양이가 볕 좋은 창가에 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is lying on the sunny window sill.
Winter sun is short but really warm.

examples.ko: 이 방은 볕이 안 들어서 조금 어두워요.
examples.en: This room gets no sun, so it is a little dark.
My face got tanned in the hot sun.

explain: '햇빛'은 해에서 오는 빛이고, '볕'은 그 빛이 주는 따뜻한 기운에 더 가까워요. 그래서 '볕이 들다', '볕을 쬐다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '햇볕'이라는 형태로 더 많이 들려요.
explain_en: 햇빛 is the light from the sun, while 볕 is closer to the warmth that light gives. It pairs with verbs such as 볕이 들다 and 볕을 쬐다. In daily speech you hear the form 햇볕 more often.

examples.en: The main product of this village is apples.
Farmers sell their produce directly at the market.
The factory's products go out nationwide.
We check the quality of the products carefully.
The weather was good this year, so there was a large yield.

examples.ko: 지역 생산물을 쓰는 식당이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More restaurants are using locally produced goods.

explain: 공장이나 농장에서 만들어 낸 물건 전체를 가리키는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 가게에서 파는 물건은 '상품', 먹을 것은 '농산물'처럼 구체적으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A rather formal word for everything made at a factory or farm. For goods sold in a shop Koreans say 상품, and for farm goods 농산물, which are more specific. 생산물 appears more in news and reports.

examples.en: I think that person and I are truly ill-fated.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 오래된 악연을 끝내기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two decided to end their long bad history.
The bad luck with this company keeps going.
There are good connections, but also bad ones.

examples.ko: 악연으로 만난 사이가 친구가 되기도 해요.
examples.en: People who met under bad circumstances sometimes become friends.

examples.ko: 저와 그 아이는 어릴 때부터 악연이었어요.
examples.en: That kid and I have been at odds since childhood.

explain: 사람과 사람 사이에 계속 나쁜 일이 생기는 관계를 말해요. '인연'은 좋고 나쁨 없이 맺어진 관계이고, '악연'은 그중 나쁜 쪽이에요. 좋은 쪽은 '좋은 인연'이라고 해요. 단순히 성격이 안 맞는 정도에는 '우리는 안 맞아요'라고 가볍게 말해요.
explain_en: A relationship in which bad things keep happening between two people. 인연 is a tie that is neither good nor bad, and 악연 is the bad kind. The good kind is called 좋은 인연. For simple incompatibility, people lightly say 우리는 안 맞아요.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우는 데 양육비가 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Raising a child costs a lot.
The government decided to support child-rearing costs.
I am saving up child-rearing money separately every month.

examples.ko: 양육비 부담 때문에 둘째를 망설이는 부부가 많아요.
examples.en: Many couples hesitate to have a second child because of the cost.

examples.ko: 이혼 후에도 부모는 양육비를 나눠 내야 해요.
examples.en: Even after divorce, parents must share the child support.
The child-rearing subsidy is going to increase this year.

explain: 아이를 키우는 데 드는 돈으로, 먹이고 입히고 돌보는 비용을 모두 포함해요. 학교와 학원에 드는 돈은 '교육비'라고 따로 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '양육비 지원', '양육비 부담'이라는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The money needed to raise a child, covering food, clothes and care. Money for school and extra classes is called 교육비 separately. In the news it appears often as 양육비 지원 or 양육비 부담.

examples.en: When the accident happened, the airbag deployed.

examples.ko: 새 차에는 에어백이 여섯 개 있어요.
examples.en: The new car has six airbags.
Thanks to the airbag, I was not badly hurt.
I went to have the driver's airbag inspected.

examples.ko: 에어백이 있어도 안전벨트는 꼭 매야 해요.
examples.en: Even with an airbag, you must wear a seat belt.

examples.ko: 차를 살 때 에어백 개수를 비교했어요.
examples.en: When buying a car, I compared the number of airbags.

explain: 자동차 사고 때 몸을 보호하는 공기주머니예요. 에어백은 안전벨트와 함께 써야 효과가 있어서, 둘을 한 쌍으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. '터지다'나 '작동하다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: An air cushion in a car that protects the body in a crash. It works properly only together with a seat belt, so the two are often mentioned as a pair. It pairs with verbs like 터지다 and 작동하다.

examples.en: That child was admitted to the hospital with malnutrition.
He went hungry for a long time and became malnourished.

examples.ko: 세계 곳곳에서 영양실조 아이들이 도움을 기다려요.
examples.en: Malnourished children around the world are waiting for help.
To prevent malnutrition you need to eat a balanced diet.

examples.ko: 무리한 다이어트가 영양실조를 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: An extreme diet can cause malnutrition.

examples.ko: 의사가 영양실조 증상을 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor explained the symptoms of malnutrition in detail.

explain: 필요한 영양을 충분히 먹지 못해서 몸이 약해진 상태예요. 보통 '영양실조에 걸리다'라고 하고, '영양부족'은 그보다 가벼운 상태에 써요. 병원 이야기나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: A condition in which the body is weak because it does not get enough nutrients. It is usually 영양실조에 걸리다, and 영양부족 is used for a milder state. You hear it in hospital talk and the news.

examples.en: I cooked the rice with green peas in it.
The child picked out only the peas to eat.

examples.ko: 마트에서 냉동 완두콩을 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of frozen peas at the mart.
When you peel the pod, peas come out in a row.
Fried rice looks nicer with peas in it.
Pea soup is smooth and sweet.

explain: '콩'의 한 종류라서 이름 끝에 '콩'이 붙어요. 초록색 알은 밥이나 볶음밥, 떡에 넣어 먹어요. '강낭콩', '검은콩' 같은 다른 콩도 많아서 색과 모양으로 구분해요.
explain_en: It ends in 콩 because it is a kind of bean. The green seeds go into rice, fried rice and rice cakes. There are many other beans such as 강낭콩 and 검은콩, which are told apart by color and shape.

examples.en: The bus driver greeted the passengers.
My father worked as a taxi driver for a long time.

examples.ko: 운전수 아저씨가 길을 잘 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The driver knows the way well.
I saw an ad looking for a truck driver.
Drivers must be careful about drowsy driving.
I heard Grandfather's house had a separate chauffeur.

explain: 직업으로 차를 모는 사람을 말하는데, '운전수'는 오래된 느낌이 있어요. 지금은 '운전기사'나 '기사님'이 더 정중해서 많이 써요. 직접 부를 때는 '기사님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a person who drives a vehicle as a job, but 운전수 sounds old-fashioned. Today 운전기사 or 기사님 is more polite and common. When addressing the person directly, say 기사님.

examples.en: I played throwing a flying disc with my dog in the park.
That athlete is a discus throw gold medalist.
The flying disc rode the wind and flew far.
On the weekend I played flying disc with friends.
The puppy ran back with the disc in its mouth.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 원반 던지는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In PE class we learned how to throw a discus.

explain: 납작하고 둥근 물건을 말해요. 놀이용 '프리스비'를 가리킬 때가 많고, 육상 경기의 '원반던지기'에서도 써요. 컴퓨터의 '디스크'는 보통 외래어 그대로 말해요.
explain_en: It means a flat round object. It often refers to a frisbee for play, and it is also used in the track event 원반던지기. For a computer disk, Koreans usually just use the loanword 디스크.

examples.en: My younger sibling talked in their sleep last night and startled me.
My husband sometimes talks loudly in his sleep.
I have a habit of talking in my sleep when tired.
That friend talked in his sleep at camp last night.

examples.ko: 잠꼬대할 때 무슨 말을 하는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I am curious what I say when I talk in my sleep.
It was cute to see the child talking in her sleep while smiling.

explain: '잠꼬대'는 명사이고 '잠꼬대하다'가 그 행동이에요. 깨어 있을 때 앞뒤가 안 맞는 말을 하면 '잠꼬대 같은 소리'라고 놀리듯 말해요. 이때는 '무슨 잠꼬대야?'처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 지금 무슨 잠꼬대 같은 소리를 하는 거예요?
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨어 있는데도 말이 앞뒤가 안 맞거나 엉뚱할 때 핀잔주듯이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to scold or tease someone who is talking nonsense while awake.

explain_en: 잠꼬대 is the noun, and 잠꼬대하다 is the action. When someone talks nonsense while awake, Koreans tease with 잠꼬대 같은 소리. You can also say 무슨 잠꼬대야? in that case.

en: eve celebration (night before a festival or event)

examples.en: Singers perform at the festival's eve event.
The university's eve festival went on until late at night.
We went to the square to see the eve festival.
The Olympics eve event was broadcast on television.
The roads were jammed because of the eve festival, so I was late.
Friends congratulated me at the pre-wedding eve party.

explain: '전야'는 행사 바로 전날 밤이고, '전야제'는 그날 밤에 미리 여는 작은 축제예요. '축제 전야제', '개막식 전야제'처럼 행사 이름 앞에 붙여 써요. 크리스마스 전날 밤은 '전야제'가 아니라 '크리스마스 이브'라고 해요.
explain_en: '전야' is the night before an event, and a '전야제' is a small celebration held that night. It goes after the event's name, as in '축제 전야제' and '개막식 전야제'. The night before Christmas is not a '전야제' but 'Christmas Eve' (크리스마스 이브).

examples.en: My uncle works in the politics desk of a newspaper.
A politics reporter delivered the news from the National Assembly.
I want to work in the society desk rather than the politics desk.
The broadcaster's politics desk got busy from dawn.
A reporter from the politics desk published a book.

examples.ko: 정치부 기사는 뉴스 맨 앞에 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Politics desk stories often come at the front of the news.

explain: 신문사나 방송국에서 정치 소식을 맡는 부서예요. 다른 부서로는 '사회부', '경제부', '문화부', '스포츠부'가 있어요. 뒤에 '기자'를 붙여 '정치부 기자'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: The department at a newspaper or broadcaster that covers political news. Other desks include 사회부, 경제부, 문화부 and 스포츠부. It is often used before 기자, as in 정치부 기자.

examples.en: The man grew a stylish mustache.

examples.ko: 아빠가 콧수염을 깎고 나니 젊어 보여요.
examples.en: Dad looks younger after shaving off his mustache.
The grandfather with a mustache is smiling.
The villain in the cartoon has a long mustache.
A mustache has to be trimmed every morning.
I got a milk mustache after drinking milk.

explain: 코 아래에 난 수염이에요. 턱에 난 수염은 '턱수염', 뺨 쪽은 '구레나룻'이라고 불러서 위치마다 이름이 달라요. '코'에 'ㅅ'이 붙어 '콧'이 되는 소리 변화도 눈여겨보세요.
explain_en: Hair growing under the nose. Chin hair is 턱수염 and sideburns are 구레나룻, so each place has its own name. Note the sound change where 코 gets an added ㅅ to become 콧.

examples.en: The brothers bicker from the morning.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 만나면 티격태격하지만 사이가 좋아요.
examples.en: Those two squabble whenever they meet, but they get along well.
The kids bickered over the order of the game.
The couple always go around together even while bickering.
I heard the sounds of squabbling from the next room.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 두 주인공은 티격태격하다가 사랑에 빠져요.
examples.en: The two leads in the drama bicker and then fall in love.

explain: 크게 싸우는 게 아니라 사소한 일로 자꾸 다투는 모습이에요. 가까운 사이라서 가볍게 다툰다는 정다운 느낌이 있어요. '싸우다'보다 약하고 '다투다'보다 더 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It shows two people repeatedly arguing over small things, not fighting hard. It has a warm tone because they are usually close. It is weaker than 싸우다 and lighter than 다투다.

examples.en: My son is a well-known rascal in the neighborhood.
The mischievous kids are playing in the dirt.

examples.ko: 그 개구쟁이가 또 창문에 공을 던졌어요.
examples.en: That rascal threw a ball at the window again.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 저는 장난이 심한 개구쟁이였어요.
examples.en: As a child I was a rascal who played a lot of pranks.
His mischievous smile is really cute.

examples.ko: 개구쟁이 동생 때문에 집이 조용할 날이 없어요.
examples.en: Because of my rascal of a brother, the house is never quiet.

explain: 장난이 심하지만 밉지 않은 아이를 귀엽게 부르는 말이에요. 나쁜 행동을 하는 '문제아'와 달리 애정이 담겨 있어요. 보통 어린 남자아이에게 많이 쓰지만 여자아이에게도 써요.
explain_en: An affectionate word for a child who plays many pranks but is not disliked. Unlike 문제아, which suggests bad behavior, 개구쟁이 carries fondness. It is most often used for young boys but also for girls.

examples.en: Wicked stepmothers often appear in old tales.
I get along well with my stepmother.
Cinderella's stepmother tormented Cinderella.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 때 계모 밑에서 자랐어요.
examples.en: He grew up with a stepmother as a child.

examples.ko: 계모라는 말에는 나쁜 인상이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The word stepmother carries a bad image.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 계모는 사실 따뜻한 사람이었어요.
examples.en: The stepmother in the drama was actually a warm person.

explain: 아버지의 새 아내를 가리키는 말이에요. 옛이야기 때문에 부정적인 이미지가 있어서, 실제로 부르거나 소개할 때는 '새어머니'를 더 많이 써요. 어머니의 새 남편은 '계부'이고, 일상에서는 '새아버지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a father's new wife. Because of old tales it has a negative image, so in real life people prefer 새어머니 when calling or introducing her. A mother's new husband is 계부, and in daily speech 새아버지.

examples.en: I practice alone while looking at a piano manual.
This guitar manual suits beginners well.

examples.ko: 서점에서 요리 교본을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cooking guidebook at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 책은 운전 교본처럼 설명이 쉬워요.
examples.en: This book explains things easily, like a driving manual.

examples.ko: 교본대로 따라 했는데도 잘 안 됐어요.
examples.en: I followed the manual exactly, but it did not work.
The teacher teaches with a manual they wrote themselves.

explain: 학교 교과서보다는 악기, 운동, 요리처럼 기술을 처음 배우는 책에 써요. 학교 수업에서는 '교과서'라고 하고, 교본은 '기본을 익히는 책'에 가까워요. 비유로 '모범'이라는 뜻으로 '교본 같은 사람'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: Rather than a school textbook, it is used for books that teach a skill from the start, such as an instrument, sport or cooking. In school lessons Koreans say 교과서. Figuratively, 교본 같은 사람 can describe a person who is a perfect model.

examples.en: In winter, cranes fly to Cheorwon.
A crane rests standing on one leg.

examples.ko: 하얀 두루미 한 쌍이 논에 내려앉았어요.
examples.en: A pair of white cranes landed in the rice field.

examples.ko: 그림 속 두루미가 날개를 활짝 폈어요.
examples.en: The crane in the painting spread its wings wide.

examples.ko: 두루미는 오래 사는 새로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: The crane is known as a long-lived bird.
The photographer went out at dawn to photograph cranes.

explain: 다리와 목이 긴 흰 새로, 오래 살고 품위 있는 새로 여겨요. 한국에서는 '학'이라고도 하는데, 옛 그림이나 이야기에서는 '학'이 더 자주 나와요. 겨울 철새라서 겨울에 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: A white bird with long legs and neck, seen as long-lived and dignified. In Korea it is also called 학, and old paintings and tales use 학 more often. It is a winter migrant, so you can meet it in winter.

examples.en: I gently cleaned my ear with a cotton swab.
I bought a box of cotton swabs at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 상처에 약을 바를 때 면봉이 편해요.
examples.en: A cotton swab is handy for putting medicine on a wound.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 면봉으로 번진 곳을 고쳐요.
examples.en: When doing makeup, I fix smudges with a cotton swab.
It is dangerous to put a cotton swab in too deep.
I throw used cotton swabs in the trash.

explain: 작은 막대 끝에 솜을 감은 물건이에요. 귀를 닦거나 약을 바를 때, 화장 고칠 때 써요. 코로나 검사에서 검체를 얻는 긴 막대는 '검체 채취용 면봉'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A small stick with cotton wrapped at the end. It is used to clean ears, apply medicine and fix makeup. The long stick used to collect samples in COVID tests is called a 검체 채취용 면봉.

examples.en: I study Korean cultural history at university.

examples.ko: 이 책은 커피의 문화사를 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: This book deals with the cultural history of coffee.
The cultural history class is the most fun.
My uncle is a professor who studies food cultural history.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 도시의 문화사를 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the museum you can see the city's cultural history at a glance.
Knowing cultural history makes travel richer.

explain: 정치나 전쟁보다 사람들의 생활, 예술, 음식, 놀이의 변화를 중심으로 본 역사예요. '정치사', '경제사'처럼 분야 이름 뒤에 '사'를 붙이는 방식이에요. 책 제목에 '~의 문화사'라는 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: History seen through changes in daily life, art, food and play rather than politics or war. It follows the pattern of 정치사 and 경제사, with 사 added to a field name. Book titles often use the form ~의 문화사.

examples.en: I caught loaches in the rice field.
Loaches are slippery and hard to catch by hand.
Chueotang is a soup made from loaches.
A loach swims along the bottom of the fish tank.
Children watched loaches at a country stream.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에 미꾸라지가 땅 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: After the rain, a loach came up onto the ground.

explain: 몸이 길고 미끄러운 민물고기로, 추어탕의 재료예요. '미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다'는 속담처럼 나쁜 사람을 비유하기도 해요. '빠져나가는 사람'을 가리킬 때도 '미꾸라지 같다'고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 질문을 하면 미꾸라지처럼 빠져나가요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤란한 상황이나 책임에서 요리조리 빠져나가는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who keeps slipping out of difficult situations or responsibility.

explain_en: A long, slippery freshwater fish used in chueotang. In the proverb 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다 it stands for one bad person. 미꾸라지 같다 also describes someone who slips out of trouble.

examples.ko: 만화 속 주인공은 눈이 큰 미소년이에요.
examples.en: The hero in the cartoon is a handsome boy with big eyes.

examples.ko: 어린 시절 그 배우는 미소년으로 유명했어요.
examples.en: As a child that actor was known as a pretty boy.
Grandmother praised that boy as a good-looking boy.

examples.ko: 그림 속 미소년이 거울을 보고 있어요.
examples.en: The handsome boy in the painting is looking in a mirror.
A pretty-boy singer appears in this novel.
He who was a handsome boy has become middle-aged before I knew it.

explain: 얼굴이 곱고 예쁘게 생긴 소년을 가리켜요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '꽃미남'이나 '잘생긴 애'가 더 자연스러워요. 만화나 소설, 옛날 영화의 인물을 말할 때 주로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a boy with a delicate, pretty face. In everyday talk today 꽃미남 or 잘생긴 애 sounds more natural. It is mostly used for characters in comics, novels and old movies.

examples.en: On Jeju Island I stayed at a small private guesthouse.
This summer I will stay at a seaside guesthouse.

examples.ko: 호텔보다 시골집에 민박하는 게 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like staying at a country house better than a hotel.
After hiking, we stayed overnight at a village guesthouse.
The landlady gave breakfast to the guests staying overnight.

examples.ko: 예약 없이 민박하려고 했는데 방이 없었어요.
examples.en: I tried to stay without a reservation, but there was no room.

explain: 일반 가정집이나 작은 집에서 돈을 내고 하룻밤 자는 것을 말해요. 호텔이나 모텔 같은 숙박업소와 다르게 주인이 사는 집인 경우가 많아요. '펜션'은 가족 단위로 빌리는 별장 느낌이라 달라요.
explain_en: It means paying to sleep a night in an ordinary home or small house. Unlike a hotel or motel, the owner often lives there. A 펜션 feels like a rented villa for families, which is different.

examples.en: The size did not fit, so I returned the clothes.
I want to return the shoes I bought online.
I called to return the broken vacuum cleaner.
If you return it within a week, you get your money back.
I gave the box to be returned to the delivery driver.

examples.ko: 포장도 뜯지 않은 물건은 반품할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Items with unopened packaging can be returned.

explain: 산 물건을 판 곳에 돌려보내는 것이에요. 가게에서 직접 바꾸는 건 '교환하다', 돈을 돌려받는 건 '환불하다'라고 해서 구분해요. 보통 '반품하고 환불받다'처럼 이어서 써요.
explain_en: It means sending a purchased item back to the seller. Swapping an item is 교환하다 and getting money back is 환불하다, so the three are distinct. They are often chained, as in 반품하고 환불받다.

examples.en: My dream is to become a ballerina.
The ballerina on stage danced gracefully.
My daughter has dreamed of being a ballerina since she was six.
A famous ballerina visited our school.
A ballerina turns standing on her toes.
After the show, we gave a bouquet to the ballerina.

explain: 여자 발레 무용수를 말하고, 남자 무용수는 '발레리노'라고 해요. 둘을 합쳐서는 '발레 무용수'나 '무용수'라고 해요. 영화나 노래에서 우아한 이미지로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means a female ballet dancer, and a male dancer is a 발레리노. Together they are called 발레 무용수 or 무용수. It often appears in films and songs as an elegant image.

examples.en: Something caught under my feet and I almost fell.
The cat is sleeping at my feet.
Watch your step. The stairs are slippery.
The fallen leaves crunched underfoot.

examples.ko: 산 위에서 보니 구름이 발밑에 있었어요.
examples.en: From the mountaintop, the clouds were below my feet.
The ground shook beneath me and I thought it was an earthquake.

explain: 서 있는 자리의 바로 아래, 발이 닿는 곳을 말해요. '발아래'와 비슷하지만 '발밑'은 가까운 바닥에 쓰고, '발아래'는 높은 곳에서 내려다보는 풍경에 더 자주 써요. '발밑을 조심하다'는 안전 안내에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It means the spot right beneath where you stand. Similar to 발아래, but 발밑 is for the nearby ground, while 발아래 is more often for a view looking down from a height. 발밑을 조심하다 is common in safety notices.

examples.en: A platinum ring is harder and rarer than gold.
We had our wedding rings made in platinum.
This necklace has diamonds set in platinum.

examples.ko: 백금은 변하지 않아서 오래 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Platinum does not tarnish, so you can use it for a long time.

examples.ko: 백금 가격이 올라서 반지 값도 올랐어요.
examples.en: The price of platinum went up, so the ring price rose too.
The factory uses platinum as a catalyst.

explain: 은빛이 도는 하얀 귀금속으로, 변색이 거의 없어요. '화이트골드'는 금에 다른 금속을 섞은 것이라 백금과 달라요. 한국에서는 '플래티넘'이라고도 하고, 시상이나 등급에도 써요.
explain_en: A silvery-white precious metal that barely tarnishes. 화이트골드 is gold mixed with other metals and is different from 백금. Koreans also say 플래티넘, which is used for awards and membership grades too.

en: separate recyclables; sort trash for recycling

examples.en: Every Sunday evening I sort the trash for recycling.
Plastic must be sorted separately.
In apartments, we sort recycling on a set day.
I learned how to sort recycling together with the kids.
I put the sorted bottles out at the recycling area.
It is better to wash things clean before sorting them for recycling.

explain: 종이, 플라스틱, 유리, 캔처럼 재활용할 쓰레기를 종류별로 나누어 버리는 것이에요. 한국에서는 아파트마다 '분리수거 하는 날'이 따로 있어요. 음식물 쓰레기는 따로 버리는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means separating recyclable trash such as paper, plastic, glass and cans by type. In Korea each apartment complex has its own 분리수거 day. Food waste is usually thrown away separately.

examples.en: Even a third-rate movie can be fun.

examples.ko: 그는 삼류 배우로 시작해서 스타가 됐어요.
examples.en: He started as a minor actor and became a star.
Don't look down on it just because it's a cheap novel.
The atmosphere of this restaurant is low-class.

examples.ko: 저는 일류보다 삼류 음악이 더 편해요.
examples.en: I find low-brow music more comfortable than top-quality music.
I read a gossip article in a trashy magazine.

explain: '일류', '이류', '삼류' 순서로 등급을 나눌 때 가장 아래쪽을 말해요. 사람이나 작품을 낮게 평가할 때 쓰는 말이라 상대에게 직접 쓰면 무례해요. 앞뒤로 '일류'와 같이 쓰면 대비가 분명해져요.
explain_en: In the ranking 일류, 이류, 삼류, it is the bottom grade. It is used to rate a person or work low, so it is rude if said to someone directly. Paired with 일류, the contrast becomes clear.

examples.ko: 과일 껍질을 벗기니 하얀 속살이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I peeled the fruit, white flesh appeared.
The skin that hasn't been in the sun is white.
I took out the clam's flesh and stir-fried it.
When you roast chestnuts, the yellow flesh is sweet.
Skin was visible through the torn pants.
The flesh of the potato turned brown.

explain: 옷이나 껍질 속에 감춰진 부드러운 부분이에요. 과일, 조개, 감자처럼 먹는 것의 안쪽에도 쓰고, 옷 속의 피부에도 써요. 피부를 말할 때는 보통 '맨살'이라고 하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: The soft part hidden inside clothes or a skin. It is used for the inside of foods such as fruit, clams and potatoes, and also for skin under clothes. For bare skin, 맨살 is often the more usual word.

examples.ko: 올해 야구 신인왕은 스무 살 투수예요.
examples.en: This year's baseball rookie of the year is a twenty-year-old pitcher.
That player won the rookie of the year title.
The candidates for rookie of the year were narrowed to three.
The pitcher won rookie of the year in his debut year.
After being chosen rookie of the year, interviews increased.

examples.ko: 골프 대회에서 신인왕에 오르는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: My goal is to win rookie of the year at the golf tour.

explain: 그해에 처음 데뷔한 선수 중 가장 뛰어난 사람에게 주는 상과 그 사람이에요. 야구나 골프 같은 스포츠에서 주로 쓰고, 가요나 연기 시상에서는 '신인상'이라고 해요. 야구와 골프 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: The award for the best newcomer of the year, and also the person who wins it. It is mostly used in sports such as baseball and golf, while for music or acting awards the word is 신인상. You often hear it in baseball and golf news.

examples.en: He was always an outsider at school.
I'm an outsider, so gatherings feel a bit uncomfortable.
The movie's hero lives as an outsider.
It is a book that looks at society through an outsider's eyes.
I try not to become an outsider at work.
Outsider artists created a new trend.

explain: 무리나 집단 안에 잘 섞이지 못하거나 밖에 있는 사람을 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '외톨이'나 '왕따'를 쓰기도 하지만 '왕따'는 괴롭힘의 의미가 강해요. '아웃사이더'는 스스로 선택한 경우에도 써서 반드시 나쁜 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: A person who does not mix with a group or stays outside it. 외톨이 and 왕따 are used for similar meaning, but 왕따 strongly implies bullying. 아웃사이더 can be a person's own choice, so it is not always negative.

examples.en: My teacher is a benefactor of my life.

examples.ko: 어려울 때 도와준 은인을 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I can't forget the benefactor who helped me in hard times.

examples.ko: 길에서 쓰러진 저를 구해 준 은인을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for the person who saved me when I collapsed on the street.
That person is a benefactor of our family.
I sent a small gift to my benefactor.
I cried when I met my benefactor.

explain: 큰 도움을 줘서 평생 고마워해야 하는 사람이에요. 가벼운 도움에는 '고마운 분'이라고 하고, '은인'은 정말 큰 은혜를 입었을 때 써요. 말할 때 자신을 낮추고 상대를 높이는 진지한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: A person who helped you so greatly that you stay grateful for life. For a small favor Koreans say 고마운 분, and 은인 is reserved for a real debt of gratitude. It is a serious word that lifts the other person up.

examples.en: My older brother enlisted as a private second class.
A private second class is the lowest rank in the army.

examples.ko: 아들이 이등병 때 쓴 편지를 아직 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the letter my son wrote when he was a private.
The private greeted the senior soldiers.
My uncle rose from private second class to sergeant.
In the movie, a private fires a gun for the first time.

explain: 한국군에서 가장 낮은 병사 계급이에요. 이등병 다음이 '일병', '상병', '병장'이에요. 군 이야기를 나눌 때 '이등병 때', '이등병 시절'이라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The lowest enlisted rank in the Korean military. After 이등병 come 일병, 상병 and 병장. When people talk about their service, they often say 이등병 때 or 이등병 시절.
